ambiguities: The initial evidence interpretation (manifest fragment and photo) borders on A2.1 (uncodified perceptual interpretation of a photograph) versus A2.4 (evaluating retrieved information) and A2.5 (fitting evidence to an abstract pattern). The interview describes the photo primarily through its documentary content and analytic fit rather than raw perceptual features, so A2.4/A2.5 are favored, but A2.1 remains a plausible secondary reading with lower confidence.

The debrief/report language choice (decision point 3) sits between A2.2 (literacy/composition) and A3.3 (selling/influencing a policy audience). Because the participant's own account frames it as a wording/composition choice about an internal estimate rather than a persuasive appeal to a specific audience's decision, A2.2 is retained as the better fit and A3.3 is not assigned.
